Main Trends of Portuguese IT Sphere

The modern economy of Portugal has gone through many stages of development, from the era of conquest and ending with the country’s accession to the EU. At the moment, the IT sphere is one of the most promising sectors in this country. IT outsourcing of Portugal developers for hire is also popular there. As it is reported by the Portuguese American Journal, this country is one of the most significant competitors in providing IT outsourcing and IT staffing services in the world. IT outsourcing Portugal is a good decision if you want to move your software development process to a foreign European country. Innovative developments are used in many spheres of public life here, including the financial sphere and the sphere of public administration. The development of the Portuguese IT sector also allows talking about increasing utilization of information and communication technology in this country. Thus, according to ICT Institute Carnegie Mellon, Portugal is one of the leaders in the usage of mobile devices which also leads to the increasing development of mobile apps.

The Popularity of Nearshoring in Portugal

There are several reasons why many companies choose nearshoring Portugal among other options. First of all, it is located in the EU, which makes it a perfect destination. There are many direct flights so the business leaders can meet and work with the team without any problems. It is also in the GMT zone, which makes nearshoring in Portugal beneficial for European countries.

The second main reason is the amount of talented and highly-professional employees. There are plenty of software development companies here with the main part of them located in Lisbon. Overall, 60% of citizens know at least one foreign language, usually English. When looking to hire developers for new business, consider partnering with startup recruiting firms for a more streamlined hiring process and keep in mind the potential advantages that come with hiring developers specifically experienced in launching new businesses.

Many European countries, namely the UK, choose to nearshore Portugal as this country shares European values and corporate culture. The political and social situation there is stable and this is always great for business. It is also a secure destination in terms of legislation and documentation. There is a transparent legislative system and a business can be registered online in three days. And the taxes here are also quite low, as the government puts effort into the development of small businesses. Among other benefits of nearshoring Lisbon are affordable rent and well-built transport and technological infrastructure.

Overall, Portuguese developers offer a high-quality products and affordable prices, that’s why companies from the UK, Germany, and the Netherlands often choose nearshoring there. It is especially popular in Great Britain because of Brexit and the growing demand for specialists that cannot be fulfilled by the internal workforce.

The Web Summit in Lisbon: A Thriving Hub of Innovation Since 2016

Web Summit has been taking place in Lisbon since 2016. The location changed from Dublin to the coast of the Iberian Peninsula. Lisbon became an ideal destination not only because of its pleasant weather and picturesque landscapes. The city, like the country as a whole, is famous for its IT professionals.

The choice to relocate the Web Summit to Lisbon improved the event’s attractiveness. It also underlined Portugal’s dedication to encouraging entrepreneurship and innovation. The Portuguese government strongly supported this event. The Web Summit was named a technologically significant event for the country.

Lisbon was an ideal location for the summit thanks to its combination of beauty and a booming technology industry. Also, additional bonuses were the accessibility of the city, developed infrastructure and relatively low cost of living. Year after year, the Lisbon Web Summit continues to push the boundaries of innovation and foster collaboration in the digital industry. Each time the event strengthens its position as a meeting place for people passionate about the entrepreneurial goals of technology.

The Industry of App Development Portugal

The software development industry is a booming sector of software development globally, and Portugal’s tech market isn’t lagging behind. With the increasing prevalence of smartphones, software development Portugal, especially app development, has seen significant growth, making it a crucial component of the software development industry.

Portugal has become a hotspot for mobile app development with a growing demand for software developers Portugal. With roughly 6.51 million smartphone users in the country, developers in Portugal are sought after to deliver competitive, high-quality services for iOS and Android platforms. They have successfully provided their expertise to businesses from around the globe, contributing to offshore software development in Portugal, and aiding the outsourcing and nearshoring economy.

Aided by supportive governmental regulations and taxation policies, Portugal has become an attractive destination for IT investments with annual IT Industry Growth Rate  1.60%. Its strategic location within Europe, fluency in English, and a thriving tech ecosystem further add to its appeal for Portugal developers.

With around 9,200 IT companies employing approximately 114,000 professionals, software development Portugal has established a solid footing. The capital city, Lisbon, remains the central hub, hosting software development Lisbon with a large portion of the IT workforce.

The industry is quite versatile, with professionals skilled in various programming languages such as PHP, ASP.NET, Python, Ruby, and Java. These technical competencies are in high demand, contributing to Portugal’s growing tech export value, which stands at an impressive $3.56 billion.
The app development industry in Portugal is thriving, with promising forecasts for the future. The total revenue in the App market is projected to reach an impressive US$394.50 million. Looking further into the future, revenue is expected to continue on this growth trajectory, with a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 7.59% from 2022 to 2027. If this prediction holds, the market volume could amount to approximately US$591.50 million by 2027.

Portugal’s English Proficiency Index score of 614 highlights a respectable level of English proficiency within the country, showcasing the effectiveness of language education and communication skills among its population.

Portugal’s Job Conditions

Portugal’s job landscape shows a good mix of industries, with a focus on tourism, agriculture and manufacturing, along with a growing focus on technology and renewable energy. Only 6.1% of the population is unemployed. 

Payroll cycles in the country follow a monthly payment schedule, with salaries paid at the end of each month. Employers must stick to specific payroll taxes. This includes contributions towards social security, healthcare and other benefits. These taxes greatly influence the overall cost of labor for businesses. 

The minimum wage in Portugal has seen slow but steady growth in recent years to support the well-being of employees. As of the most recent data, the minimum rate stands at around $775 per month. Overtime pay is set by labor laws (Constituição da República Portuguesa), ensuring that employees receive extra money for any more hours worked. And, often, this is at a higher rate than their standard wage.

Employee benefits are a very important part of the staff framework in the country. Many companies offer comprehensive health insurance, paid leave and retirement plans. These benefits are designed to enhance employee satisfaction and foster a healthy work environment.

Diverse Tech Hubs in Portugal: A Closer Look at Cities

The dynamic landscape of the software development industry in Portugal is spread across several cities, each boasting its unique strengths and opportunities. Let’s delve into the specifics of these tech hubs, exploring the thriving environment for software developers in Portugal.

  • Lisbon

Lisbon, the capital of Portugal, has emerged as a vibrant tech hub, home to software developers Lisbon, with an estimated 1,000 software developers as of now. These professionals have been drawn to the city’s dynamic tech scene and the competitive salaries from €45,000 to €60,000 annually.

  • Porto

Known for its vibrant tech scene, Porto has seen an impressive growth in its tech industry. The average annual remuneration for software developer Porto varied between €30,000 and €45,000. About 1500 software developers are currently working in Porto.

  • Vila Nova de Gaia

Sharing its border with Porto, Vila Nova de Gaia benefits from its proximity to one of the country’s tech hotspots. About 350 software developers in this region could expect to earn an average salary ranging from €40,000 to €60,000 annually.

  • Amadora

As part of the Greater Lisbon metropolitan area, Amadora also has a significant tech scene. The average salary for software developers was in the ballpark of €25,000 to €49,000 annually. About 400 developers are now living in this area.

  • Braga

Braga’s tech sector has been steadily growing, drawing an increasing number of software developers to the city. The average salary for software developers varied from €25,000 to €40,000 annually. The developer population was trending upwards in line with the burgeoning tech industry: more than 700 software engineers are now living and working in Braga.

Regulatory Requirements

In Portugal and Ukraine, the hiring process is governed by labor laws that outline regulations regarding work hours, vacation days, contract termination, and more. Both countries also have stringent anti-discrimination laws to ensure fairness in hiring. Importantly, compliance with GDPR is required when dealing with employees’ personal data in Portugal.

For Intellectual Property (IP) protection, both Portugal and Ukraine have comprehensive legal frameworks adhering to international standards. Portugal’s IP protection aligns with EU regulations, while Ukraine’s is in accordance with international treaties such as the Paris Convention and the Berne Convention. 

However, specific nuances within each country’s laws necessitate seeking local legal advice for optimal IP protection. In both hiring and IP protection, understanding and complying with local legal landscapes is crucial when expanding or outsourcing operations in either country.

FAQs

  • Where does Portugal stand in terms of its technological landscape?

As a result of the country’s emphasis on new ideas and business creation, Portugal’s IT sector is booming. Numerous established and up-and-coming technology businesses have opened operations in Portugal. This is due in large part to the country’s abundance of tech hotspots like Lisbon and Porto. Increased need for qualified developers is a direct effect of this expansion.

  • How does the culture in Portugal influence the selection of software engineers?

The Portuguese cultural tradition places a premium on honesty, teamwork, and a healthy work-life equilibrium. Portugal has a more laid-back approach to the workplace, with a priority on quality rather than haste. The benefits of this for businesses that need to hire developers include potentially higher-quality output and a more pleasant office environment.

  • How would you describe the Portuguese educational system?

Portugal’s education system is among the best in the world, including numerous top-tier institutions and institutes of higher technology. Courses and degrees in computer science and related topics can be found at many of these schools. This means that many Portuguese programmers have a solid educational background and set of skills.

  • Which fields or kinds of work are most suited for Portuguese programmers?

Developers from Portugal are adaptable and capable of working on a wide variety of projects, from web and mobile apps to machine learning and artificial intelligence. Developers with experience in the financial technology and e-commerce sectors would do well to look for work in Portugal.

  • Where can I learn about the steps required to hire a programmer in Portugal?

The assistance of a recruiting agency are commonplace components of the Portuguese hiring process, however variations exist. Education, work history, technical aptitude, and cultural compatibility are only some of the factors considered throughout the hiring process. Potential employees’ technical skills could be evaluated through interviews or competitions. The most qualified candidate is then chosen for the position.
